name: Classical Antiquity (Greece & Rome)
summary: Greek sculptors develop the idealised, naturalistic human body, contrapposto and canons of proportion. Most Greek bronzes are lost and survive through Roman marble copies, which shaped every later classical revival.
image_file: 02 10 2024 Photo Paolo Villa-Napoli-mann-Museo Archeologico-FO232526tris-Arte Greca copia romana-Policleto Doriforo Polykleitos Doryphoros from Pompeii-marmo marble carrara.jpg
image_caption: Polykleitos, Doryphoros (Spear-Bearer), Roman marble copy from Pompeii, National Archaeological Museum, Naples

name: Late Gothic & Proto-Renaissance
summary: Painters begin to break from flat Byzantine conventions, giving figures weight, emotion and a believable space to inhabit. Giotto is the pivotal figure.
image_file: Compianto sul Cristo morto.jpg
image_caption: Giotto, Lamentation, Scrovegni Chapel, Padua, c. 1305

name: Early Italian Renaissance
summary: Florence leads a revival of classical antiquity: linear perspective, anatomical study and free-standing sculpture return, funded by patrons such as the Medici.
image_file: The Tribute Money by Masaccio.jpg
image_caption: Masaccio, The Tribute Money, Brancacci Chapel, Florence, c. 1425

name: Northern Renaissance
summary: In Flanders, the Netherlands and Germany, artists perfect oil painting and pursue minute detail, rich symbolism and scenes of everyday and moral life.
image_file: The Arnolfini portrait (1434).jpg
image_caption: Jan van Eyck, Arnolfini Portrait, 1434

name: High Renaissance
summary: A short peak of balance and harmony centred on Rome, Florence, Milan and Venice, defined by Leonardo, Michelangelo, Raphael and Titian.
image_file: "The School of Athens" by Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino.jpg
image_caption: Raphael, The School of Athens, 1509–11

name: Mannerism
summary: A reaction to High Renaissance calm: elongated figures, unstable compositions, acid colour and deliberate artifice.
image_file: Parmigianino - Madonna and Child with Angels, known as the Madonna with the Long Neck.jpg
image_caption: Parmigianino, Madonna with the Long Neck, c. 1534–40

name: Baroque
summary: Drama, movement and strong light-and-shadow (chiaroscuro). Catholic Baroque aims to overwhelm the faithful; Dutch Golden Age painting turns to portraits, interiors and civic life.
image_file: Caravaggio — The Calling of Saint Matthew.jpg
image_caption: Caravaggio, The Calling of Saint Matthew, 1599–1600

name: Rococo
summary: A lighter, playful French court style of pastel colour, curving ornament, love and leisure.
image_file: The Swing (P430).jpg
image_caption: Jean-Honoré Fragonard, The Swing, 1767

name: Neoclassicism
summary: Inspired by excavations at Pompeii and Enlightenment ideals, artists return to clear line, civic virtue and Greco-Roman subjects.
image_file: Le Serment des Horaces - Jacques-Louis David - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 3692 ; MR 1432.jpg
image_caption: Jacques-Louis David, Oath of the Horatii, 1784

name: Romanticism
summary: Emotion, the sublime power of nature, national struggle and the individual imagination take priority over reason and rules.
image_file: Caspar David Friedrich - Wanderer above the Sea of Fog.jpeg
image_caption: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, c. 1818

name: Realism
summary: Artists reject idealised history painting and depict ordinary people, labour and contemporary life as they are.
image_file: Jean-François Millet - Gleaners - Google Art Project 2.jpg
image_caption: Jean-François Millet, The Gleaners, 1857

name: Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
summary: Young English painters reject academic convention for brilliant colour, minute natural detail and medieval, literary and moral subjects.
image_file: John Everett Millais - Ophelia - Google Art Project.jpg
image_caption: John Everett Millais, Ophelia, 1851–52

name: Impressionism
summary: Painting outdoors with broken brushwork to capture light, weather and fleeting modern Paris; named after Monet's 'Impression, Sunrise'.
image_file: Monet - Impression, Sunrise.jpg
image_caption: Claude Monet, Impression, Sunrise, 1872

name: Post-Impressionism
summary: Painters push past Impressionism toward structure (Cézanne), science (Seurat), symbolism (Gauguin) and expressive colour (Van Gogh).
image_file: Van Gogh - Starry Night - Google Art Project.jpg
image_caption: Vincent van Gogh, The Starry Night, 1889

name: Symbolism & Art Nouveau
summary: Dream, myth, eroticism and anxiety expressed through ornament and symbolic form; Vienna Secession and Nordic angst.
image_file: The Kiss - Gustav Klimt - Google Cultural Institute.jpg
image_caption: Gustav Klimt, The Kiss, 1907–08

name: Fauvism & Expressionism
summary: Colour is freed from description and used for emotional and decorative force.
image_file: Kirchner - Street, Dresden, 1908, 12.1951.jpg
image_caption: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Street, Dresden, 1908 (reworked 1919)

name: Cubism
summary: Picasso and Braque fracture objects into facets and multiple viewpoints, ending single-point perspective.
image_file: Juan Gris - Portrait of Pablo Picasso - Google Art Project.jpg
image_caption: Juan Gris, Portrait of Pablo Picasso, 1912

name: Futurism
summary: An Italian avant-garde that glorifies speed, machines, the city and violent modernity, trying to show motion and energy in paint and bronze.
image_file: 'Unique Forms of Continuity in Space', 1913 bronze by Umberto Boccioni.jpg
image_caption: Umberto Boccioni, Unique Forms of Continuity in Space, 1913

name: Early Abstraction
summary: Art without recognisable subject matter: Kandinsky's spiritual colour music and Mondrian's grid of primaries.
image_file: Composition VII - Wassily Kandinsky, GAC.jpg
image_caption: Wassily Kandinsky, Composition VII, 1913

name: Dada & Surrealism
summary: Dada attacks the very idea of art after WWI; Surrealism mines dreams and the unconscious.
image_file: Marcel Duchamp, 1917, Fountain, photograph by Alfred Stieglitz.jpg
image_caption: Marcel Duchamp's Fountain (1917), photographed by Alfred Stieglitz for The Blind Man, 1917

name: American Modernism
summary: American artists portray the modern city and its isolation in a clear, realist idiom.
image_file: Grant Wood - American Gothic (1930).jpg
image_caption: Grant Wood, American Gothic, 1930

name: Abstract Expressionism
summary: New York becomes the art capital; gesture (Pollock) and colour field (Rothko) on monumental canvases.

name: Pop Art
summary: Advertising, comics, celebrity and mass production become the subjects and methods of fine art.

name: Neo-Expressionism
summary: A return to raw, figurative and gestural painting after Minimalism and Conceptual art, linked to street culture in New York and history in Germany.
